questions.question: How many players does each team have on the pitch at the start of a football match?
questions.explanation: That is ten outfield players plus one goalkeeper.

questions.question: What colour card does a referee show to send a player off?
questions.explanation: Red and yellow cards were first used at the 1970 World Cup in Mexico.

questions.question: What is the nickname of the England women's football team?
questions.explanation: The name is a nod to the three lions on the England badge, which is why the men's team is called the Three Lions.

questions.question: What is it called when one player scores three goals in a single match?
questions.explanation: The phrase is thought to come from cricket, where a bowler who took three wickets with three balls was once given a new hat.

questions.question: Which country did Lionel Messi captain to victory at the 2022 World Cup?
questions.explanation: Argentina beat France on penalties after a thrilling 3–3 draw in the final in Qatar.

questions.question: Which club plays its home games at Anfield?
questions.explanation: Funnily enough, Anfield was Everton's home first, until they moved out in 1892 and Liverpool were formed to play there.

questions.question: Which club is nicknamed 'the Gunners'?
questions.explanation: Arsenal were founded in 1886 by workers at the Royal Arsenal, a weapons factory in Woolwich.

questions.question: In 2025, England's women kept their European title by beating which country in the final?
questions.explanation: The final in Basel finished 1–1, and Chloe Kelly scored the winning penalty in the shoot-out.

questions.question: Which football ground is nicknamed 'the Theatre of Dreams'?
questions.explanation: Manchester United legend Sir Bobby Charlton gave Old Trafford its famous nickname.

questions.question: What does VAR stand for in football?
questions.explanation: The VAR team watches replays on screens and can tell the referee to take another look.

questions.question: In March 2023, who became the England men's team's all-time top goalscorer?
questions.explanation: Kane scored a penalty against Italy for his 54th England goal, one more than Wayne Rooney's old record.

questions.question: Which country hosted the men's World Cup in 1966 and won it?
questions.explanation: England beat West Germany 4–2 at Wembley, with Geoff Hurst scoring a hat-trick.

questions.question: How far from the goal line is the penalty spot?
questions.explanation: Twelve yards is about 11 metres, roughly the length of a double-decker bus.

questions.question: Which country hosted the very first World Cup, in 1930?
questions.explanation: Uruguay hosted it and won it too, beating Argentina 4–2 in the final.

questions.question: Where was the 2023 Women's World Cup held?
questions.explanation: It was the first Women's World Cup with two host countries, and Spain beat England in the final in Sydney.

questions.question: By the end of the 2022 tournament, which country had won the men's World Cup the most times?
questions.explanation: Brazil won it five times: in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002.

questions.question: Who managed England's women to European Championship titles in both 2022 and 2025?
questions.explanation: Wiegman had already won the Euros with her home country, the Netherlands, in 2017.

questions.question: Which club won the Premier League in 2015–16, having started the season as 5000–1 outsiders?
questions.explanation: Claudio Ranieri's side finished ten points clear in one of the greatest upsets in sporting history.

questions.question: Who scored the 'Hand of God' goal against England at the 1986 World Cup?
questions.explanation: Four minutes later he scored a dazzling solo goal that fans later voted the Goal of the Century.

questions.question: Which country beat England in the final of Euro 2020, played at Wembley in 2021?
questions.explanation: The final ended 1–1 and Italy won the penalty shoot-out 3–2.

questions.question: What nickname was given to Arsenal's side that went the whole 2003–04 Premier League season unbeaten?
questions.explanation: They won 26 and drew 12 of their 38 league games.

questions.question: By the end of the 2024–25 season, who was the Premier League's all-time top goalscorer?
questions.explanation: Shearer scored 260 Premier League goals for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle United.

questions.question: Under the laws of the game, you cannot be offside if a team-mate plays the ball straight to you from which of these?
questions.explanation: There is no offside straight from a throw-in, a goal kick or a corner.

questions.question: What was introduced in 1992 to stop goalkeepers picking up a deliberate kick from a team-mate?
questions.explanation: It followed a cagey, time-wasting 1990 World Cup that had very few goals.

questions.question: In 1968, which became the first English club to win the European Cup?
questions.explanation: They beat Benfica 4–1 after extra time at Wembley, ten years after the Munich air disaster.

questions.question: At the 1990 World Cup, which country knocked England out on penalties in the semi-final?
questions.explanation: It was the night of Paul Gascoigne's tears, and West Germany went on to win the final.

questions.question: Which country won the first Women's World Cup, held in China in 1991?
questions.explanation: The USA beat Norway 2–1 in the final in Guangzhou.

questions.question: Sergio Agüero's last-gasp goal in May 2012 won Manchester City the title in a 3–2 win against which side?
questions.explanation: It was City's first league title in 44 years, snatched from Manchester United on goal difference.

questions.question: Which French referee became the first woman to referee a men's World Cup match, in 2022?
questions.explanation: She took charge of Costa Rica against Germany in Qatar, with two women as her assistants.

questions.question: Roughly how many fans watched England beat Germany in the Women's Euro 2022 final at Wembley?
questions.explanation: The crowd of 87,192 was a record for any European Championship match, men's or women's.

questions.question: Months before the 1966 World Cup, the stolen trophy was found wrapped in newspaper by a dog. What was the dog called?
questions.explanation: Pickles, a collie, sniffed out the parcel under a hedge while on a walk with his owner, and became a national hero.

questions.question: In 1863, the Football Association met to write the first rules of the game in which kind of place?
questions.explanation: Club captains met at the Freemasons' Tavern in London, and the rules they agreed are the roots of today's game.

questions.question: Which club is nicknamed 'the Canaries'?
questions.explanation: Norwich has a long history of breeding canaries, brought there by Flemish weavers who settled in the city centuries ago.

questions.question: Goal machine Erling Haaland plays for which country?
questions.explanation: He was actually born in Leeds, while his dad Alf-Inge was playing for Leeds United.

questions.question: Which country's football team plays in bright orange shirts?
questions.explanation: Orange honours the Dutch royal family, the House of Orange-Nassau, even though the Dutch flag has no orange in it.

questions.question: What size of football is used in grown-up matches?
questions.explanation: Younger children often play with a smaller size 3 or size 4 ball.

questions.question: What does it mean when a goalkeeper keeps a 'clean sheet'?
options: Their team lets in no goals
questions.answer: Their team lets in no goals
questions.explanation: The defenders share the credit too, because nobody has managed to score against them.

questions.question: Which London club plays at Craven Cottage, right beside the River Thames?
questions.explanation: The ground is named after a real cottage that once stood there, and a little pavilion called the Cottage still sits in one corner.

questions.question: Which country's women's football team is nicknamed 'the Matildas'?
questions.explanation: The name comes from the much-loved Australian folk song 'Waltzing Matilda'.

questions.question: Which country's football team is nicknamed 'Les Bleus', meaning 'the Blues'?
questions.explanation: Their blue shirts match the blue on the French flag.

questions.question: How long is a normal professional football match, not counting extra time or added time?
questions.explanation: Two halves of 45 minutes, with a break at half-time.

questions.question: Stamford Bridge is the home ground of which London club?
questions.explanation: It has been Chelsea's home since the club was founded in 1905.

questions.question: How many points does a team get for winning a Premier League match?
questions.explanation: A draw earns 1 point, and a loss earns nothing.

questions.question: Which country won the men's World Cup in 2018?
questions.explanation: They beat Croatia 4–2 in the final in Moscow, with a 19-year-old Kylian Mbappé scoring.

questions.question: Which country won its fourth men's World Cup in 2014?
questions.explanation: Mario Götze scored the winner against Argentina in extra time in Rio de Janeiro.

questions.question: Which footballer is known by the nickname 'CR7'?
questions.explanation: His initials and his famous number 7 shirt.

questions.question: The 2026 men's World Cup was hosted by the USA, Canada and which other country?
questions.explanation: It was the first World Cup shared by three countries, and the first with 48 teams.

questions.question: Which club did David Beckham join when he left Manchester United in 2003?
questions.explanation: He moved to LA Galaxy later, in 2007.

questions.question: In which city is the San Siro stadium?
questions.explanation: AC Milan and Inter Milan share it, so the city's derby is played at the same ground both ways.

questions.question: How many World Cups did Pelé win as a player with Brazil?
questions.explanation: 1958, 1962 and 1970: he is the only player to win three.

questions.question: Who scored a hat-trick for England in the 1966 World Cup final?
questions.explanation: His third goal came as fans ran on to the pitch: 'They think it's all over... it is now!'

questions.question: Which club won the first Premier League title, in 1992–93?
questions.explanation: It was their first league title for 26 years.

questions.question: Kenny Dalglish managed which club to the Premier League title in 1994–95?
questions.explanation: Steel magnate Jack Walker's millions and Alan Shearer's 34 goals brought the title to Ewood Park.

questions.question: Brian Clough led which club to two European Cups, in 1979 and 1980?
questions.explanation: Forest had only been promoted to the top division in 1977.

questions.question: Which Welsh player won the Champions League five times with Real Madrid?
questions.explanation: His overhead kick in the 2018 final against Liverpool is one of the great final goals.
